Description: Additional KG product accessible (embeddings, paths)
Notes: No equivalent in dataset-level frameworks; derived products are a KG-specific concept

Description: API, Neo4j, or other hosted graph database accessible
Source: Adapted — FAIR (A1); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026)
Notes: FAIR A1 calls for retrieval via a standardized protocol; HCLS recommends void:sparqlEndpoint and Mohammadi et al. include SPARQL endpoint and REST API elements. We extend this to graph-native access (e.g., Neo4j)

Description: Multiple ways to download or access
Source: Adapted — FAIR (A1); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026)
Notes: HCLS dcat:accessURL/dcat:downloadURL and Mohammadi et al. "distributions" describe multiple access routes; we score whether more than one exists

Description: Source code for making the KG is publicly accessible
Notes: O3: version control and permissively license code

Description: KG is downloadable in its entirety
Source: Adapted — FAIR (A1.1); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026)
Notes: HCLS dcat:downloadURL (distribution level) and Mohammadi et al. download URL; we require the full graph, not a subset

Principle: B. Provenance of Nodes and Edges
Description: List of sources provided
Notes: HCLS dct:source / prov:wasDerivedFrom (source datasets); Mohammadi et al. primary source and references

Description: Sources have versions/dates/file names used
Notes: HCLS pav:retrievedFrom and source-dataset versions support this; we require versions, dates or file names for every source. Mohammadi et al. record sources but not their versions

Description: Import dependencies declared
Notes: HCLS pav:createdWith records software used to create a dataset; O3 recommends maintainer-friendly, reproducible code. We require declared import dependencies

Description: Nodes and edges have source information
Notes: FAIR R1.2 calls for detailed provenance; HCLS and Mohammadi et al. record provenance only at the dataset level, so node- and edge-level source attribution is our extension

Description: Duplicate edge management taken into consideration
Notes: Edge-level construct with no equivalent in flat-dataset schemas

Description: Provenance of edge creation
Notes: Edge-level provenance of how each relationship is generated; no equivalent in dataset-level schemas

Description: Schema for how edge types are created; where they are coming from
Notes: Edge-type derivation rules; dataset-level schemas record vocabularies used but not how edge types are created

Principle: C. Documented Standards, Schema, and Construction
Description: Entities/nodes human-readable and usable outside the KG
Notes: FAIR R1 (richly described with relevant attributes) and R1.3 (domain-relevant community standards)

Description: Identifiers support entity resolution
Source: Adapted — FAIR (F1, I3); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026)
Notes: HCLS idot:preferredPrefix / idot:identifierPattern; Mohammadi et al. namespace and IRI template

Description: Documentation on construction provided
Notes: Process-level transparency beyond what metadata schemas specify; HCLS foaf:page and Mohammadi et al. home page link to general documentation but do not require construction documentation

Description: Documented data transforms
Notes: No metadata element records data transforms applied during construction

Description: Uses a documented schema for construction
Source: Adapted — HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026); FAIR (I2)
Notes: HCLS dct:conformsTo and void:vocabulary; Mohammadi et al. vocabulary, conforms to and meta graph

Description: Clearly identified stable versions
Notes: HCLS pav:version (required at version level); Mohammadi et al. version element

Description: Public tracker for requests
Notes: O3 recommends public issue trackers and searchable discussion channels rather than private email; also an OBO Foundry principle (responsiveness)

Description: Contact indicated (organization or person)
Source: Adapted — HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026); TRUST (User focus)
Notes: HCLS dct:publisher (required); Mohammadi et al. publisher/creator with role, name and email

Description: Updated more than once per year
Notes: HCLS recommends recording update frequency; the threshold of more than one update per year is new to this framework (Bonner et al. 2022 also identified irregular updates as a gap)

Description: Prior versions accessible with documented changes
Notes: HCLS pav:previousVersion links versions; TRUST Sustainability covers continued access to holdings. Documented changes between versions are our addition

Principle: E. Evaluation by Metrics and Fitness for Purpose
Description: Case study/example of use provided
Notes: Mohammadi et al. include sample queries and example resources, but not a use case or case study

Description: KG utility evaluated against other methods
Notes: Assesses whether evaluation is reported, not the content-accuracy assessment itself (contrast Wang et al. 2021; Xue & Zou 2023)

Description: Clearly defined scope
Source: Adapted — TRUST (Transparency); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026)
Notes: TRUST Transparency asks repositories to state their mission and scope; HCLS dct:description and Mohammadi et al. description/theme describe content. We require an explicit statement of intended scope

Description: Multiple types of evaluation methods
Notes: Reporting-level; distinct from Wang et al. (2021) and Xue & Zou (2023), who directly assess content quality

Description: One or more ways of measuring accuracy/confidence
Notes: Reporting-level; distinct from Wang et al./Xue & Zou, who directly measure accuracy

Description: KG licensing status (specific open license, proprietary/subscription-based, or unclear/not stated)
Source: Adapted — FAIR (R1.1); HCLS; Mohammadi et al. (2026); O3
Notes: FAIR R1.1, HCLS dct:license, Mohammadi et al. license, O3 permissive licensing. Recorded as a licensing category rather than yes/no
